name: San Marino

fees.name: Schengen short-stay visa (via Italy, required for entry to San Marino)
fees.applies: nationalities requiring a Schengen visa to enter Italy/Schengen area (San Marino issues no visa of its own; it is landlocked within Italy and has no independent border control, so entry is governed by the Schengen short-stay visa processed at an Italian consulate/embassy)
fees.notes: San Marino does not operate its own visa regime for general travellers; travellers who need a visa to enter must obtain a Schengen visa from an Italian diplomatic mission, since San Marino cannot be reached without transiting Schengen territory. The European Commission confirmed the standard adult Schengen visa fee rose from EUR 80 to EUR 90 effective 11 June 2026 (Regulation (EC) 810/2009 as amended).

fees.name: Schengen short-stay visa - child fee (age 6-12)
fees.applies: children aged 6-12 of nationalities requiring a Schengen visa

vfs.note: Schengen visa applications for entry into the San Marino area are processed through Italian consulates/embassies (and their contracted visa application centres, which vary by country of application, e.g. VFS Global in some jurisdictions for Italy). No dedicated San Marino VFS operation exists; could not verify a specific San Marino-labelled outsourced-centre service fee on an official source.

free_visa_notes: San Marino is an enclave surrounded entirely by Italy with no independent border control or airport handling scheduled international flights; it cannot be reached without transiting the Schengen Area. It does not issue its own visas for general tourism - travellers who are visa-exempt for Schengen/Italy (including US, UK, Canadian, most nationalities) can visit San Marino without any visa or fee. Travellers who require a visa to enter the Schengen Area must obtain a standard Schengen short-stay visa (processed via an Italian consulate) to visit San Marino; no separate San Marino-specific fee exists. From late 2026, visa-exempt nationals will also need an ETIA travel authorisation (EUR 20, EU-wide, not San Marino specific) to enter Schengen territory including San Marino - excluded from 'fees' above per scope (eTA/ETIAS is an EU-wide instrument, not a San Marino national scheme) but noted here for completeness. Reciprocity fee variations (IND, USA, GBR, CHN, NGA, PAK, PHL, BGD, RUS, CAN) could not be separately verified for San Marino because it does not run its own reciprocity fee schedule; the applicable schedule is Italy's/EU's standard Schengen visa fee table, which does not vary by nationality except for a small number of facilitation-agreement countries (fee reductions/waivers for certain former USSR states, not applicable to the ten reference nationalities).
